scene_evidence_records.topic: The Devil's Den photograph, "Home of a Rebel Sharpshooter" (B.6.6)
scene_evidence_records.printed: The photograph is staged. It was taken on 6 July 1863, per Frassanito attributed to Timothy O'Sullivan, with Gardner arriving 5 July and later claiming credit. The body of an unidentified Confederate was moved more than 40 yards to the stone niche (the same body appears in another photograph), a prop rifle was placed (a type a sharpshooter would not use, and it appears in other Gardner photographs), a blanket under the body may have been used to carry it, and Gardner's caption (mortal wound from a shell, a November return) is considered implausible. The Library of Congress record calls the setting a "rocky niche"; the wall was built by Confederates and later rebuilt by the NPS ([Wiki-HomeRebel], [Prologue]). Consequences for the animation: do not stage a "sharpshooter's lair" scene on the strength of this photograph; use it as evidence of the terrain and of a body, not of a sniper's life. Open: the dead man's clothing is not described in the retrieved sources (LOC record and Frassanito's "Gettysburg: A Journey in Time" are the places to look) and the prop rifle's type is unverified.
scene_evidence_records.rule: no 'sharpshooter's lair' scene; the dead man's clothing and the prop rifle are open (G15): no kit record may be invented for them
